project.title: Structural surfaceomics of myeloma models to identify tumor-specific protein conformations
project.projectDescription: Proteins at the cell surface are promising targets for cancer immunotherapies. While standard surface proteomics can be powerful for target discovery, even more fruitful is identifying cancer-specific surface protein features. To this end, we recently described a technology to identify cancer-specific protein three-dimensional conformations. In “structural surfaceomics”, we integrated XL-MS and surface protein biotinylation to identify the active conformation of integrin beta-2 as a promising cellular therapy target in acute myeloid leukemia (Mandal et al, Nature Cancer (2023)). However, we only applied structural surfaceomics to a single cancer model, and crosslink modeling was done manually. Here, we apply our technology to additional cancer models and implement an automated pipeline for crosslink characterization, AlphaCross-XL (Biswas et al, ASMS abstract (2023)).
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Myeloma cells (AMO1) were harvested in batches for a total of 2.4 billion. Cell surfaces were crosslinked with 10 mM PhoX or DSSO. Cell surface glycans were oxidized then biotinylated. After lysis, proteins were captured on streptavidin beads, digested (trypsin/lysC), then eluted from desalting columns with 80% ACN + 0.1% TFA, followed by Ni2+-NTA enrichment with 30% NH4OH elutions. Peptides were subjected to high pH reverse phase chromatography before LC-MS/MS analysis on a timsTOF Pro mass spectrometer with a 60 min LC gradient in 11-26% ACN range before a quick ramp up to 100%. Crosslinked peptides were mapped to proteins from our myeloma surfaceome database using pLink2 and proteins mapped to AlphaFold structures with AlphaCross-XL and distance thresholds analyzed.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data (.d) files were converted to .mgf files for analysis. Crosslinked peptides were mapped to proteins from our myeloma and prostate surfaceome database using pLink2 and proteins mapped to AlphaFold structures with AlphaCross-XL and distance thresholds analyzed.
keywords: Cell surface proteomics; xl-ms; crosslinking mass spectrometry; structural biology; protein structure
